courseTitle: History on Our Doorstep — Local History Detective Toolkit (Roman Towns to Living Memory)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: Local History Toolkit
root.gloss: Universal UK Local History Detective Toolkit — uniting place-names, 1880s Ordnance Survey maps, High Street architecture, Censuses, School Logbooks, canals, War Memorials, and living oral history.

children.label: 1. Maps, Names and Buildings
children.gloss: Place-Name Settler Clues → Victorian Ordnance Survey Maps → Stone Benchmarks and Trig Pillars • Tudor Timber and Jetties → Georgian Sash vs Victorian Brick → Cyphers, Datestones and Ghost Signs

children.label: 1. Secret Code in Place-Names and Old Ordnance Survey Maps
children.q2Chain: Place-Name Settler Clues → Victorian Ordnance Survey Maps → Stone Benchmarks and Trig Pillars
children.gloss: Place-Name Settler Clues → Victorian Ordnance Survey Maps → Stone Benchmarks and Trig Pillars

children.label: Place-Name Settler Clues
children.gloss: Roman castra forts (-chester), Anglo-Saxon homesteads (-ham, -ton, -ford), and Viking villages (-by) left lasting clues recorded in the 1086 Domesday Book.

children.label: castra
children.gloss: Latin word for a walled Roman; fort behind -chester and -caster.

children.label: Latin word for a walled Roman
children.gloss: Latin word for a walled Roman

children.label: homesteads
children.gloss: Anglo-Saxon family farms remembered in; -ham and -ton names.

children.label: → Domesday Book
children.gloss: King William’s 1086 survey naming; over 13,000 English places.

children.label: Victorian Ordnance Survey Maps
children.gloss: Founded in 1791, the Ordnance Survey published detailed 1880s Victorian parish and town maps recording every street, mill, and field.

children.label: Ordnance Survey
children.gloss: Britain’s national mapping agency; founded in 1791.

children.label: vanished mills
children.gloss: Lost workplaces and ponds still; visible on 1880s town maps.

children.label: → Gloucester
children.gloss: Historic city whose 1880s OS plan; shows old churches and banks.

children.label: Stone Benchmarks and Trig Pillars
children.gloss: Surveyors chiseled broad-arrow benchmarks into stone walls for exact sea-level heights and built hilltop concrete trig pillars from 1936.

children.label: broad arrow
children.gloss: Three-line upward symbol carved beneath; a stone benchmark bar.

children.label: trig pillars
children.gloss: White concrete hilltop columns built; from 1936 for sighting angles.

children.label: → surveyors
children.gloss: Map-makers who measured exact heights; and triangle angles outdoors.

children.label: 2. Reading Buildings on the High Street
children.q2Chain: Tudor Timber and Jetties → Georgian Sash vs Victorian Brick → Cyphers, Datestones and Ghost Signs
children.gloss: Tudor Timber and Jetties → Georgian Sash vs Victorian Brick → Cyphers, Datestones and Ghost Signs

children.label: Tudor Timber and Jetties
children.gloss: Looking above modern shopfronts reveals medieval stone churches and Tudor oak-beamed houses with wattle-and-daub panels and overhanging upper jetties.

children.label: oak timber
children.gloss: Heavy wooden beams pegged together; to frame Tudor town houses.

children.label: upper jetty
children.gloss: Overhanging top floor jutting out; to make extra space upstairs.

children.label: → wattle and daub
children.gloss: Woven sticks and plaster filling; spaces between dark Tudor beams.

children.label: Georgian Sash vs Victorian Brick
children.gloss: Georgian streets prized calm symmetry and sliding sash windows, whereas Victorian railways brought bright machine-made red brick, terracotta, and bay windows.

children.label: sash windows
children.gloss: Tall Georgian wooden window frames sliding; up and down on cords.

children.label: Tall Georgian wooden window frames sliding
children.gloss: Tall Georgian wooden window frames sliding

children.label: red brick
children.gloss: Bright machine-made Victorian bricks; carried cheaply by train.

children.label: → terracotta
children.gloss: Moulded baked clay ornament; decorating grand Victorian halls.

children.label: Cyphers, Datestones and Ghost Signs
children.gloss: Cast-iron postbox royal cyphers (like V.R. and G.R.), doorway datestones, and faded brick ghost signs date streets and lost shops.

children.label: royal cyphers
children.gloss: Monarchs’ initials like V.R. or; G.R. cast onto red postboxes.

children.label: datestones
children.gloss: Carved stone plaques recording the; year and original building name.

children.label: → ghost signs
children.gloss: Faded hand-painted adverts surviving high; on old brick walls.

children.label: 2. Families, Schools and Work
children.gloss: The Ten-Year UK Census → Parish Books and Headstones → Victorian School Logbooks • Market Halls and Milestones → Canals, Locks and Watermills → Steam Stations and Street Names

children.label: 3. Who Lived in Number 12? Censuses, Parish Books and School Logbooks
children.q2Chain: The Ten-Year UK Census → Parish Books and Headstones → Victorian School Logbooks
children.gloss: The Ten-Year UK Census → Parish Books and Headstones → Victorian School Logbooks

children.label: The Ten-Year UK Census
children.gloss: Held every ten years since 1801 (naming everyone from 1841), UK Censuses record household ages, birthplaces, and vanished jobs like ostlers and lamplighters.

children.label: enumerators
children.gloss: Local officers who walked door; to door copying Census schedules.

children.label: occupations
children.gloss: Jobs column listing carpenters,; servants, ostlers, and lamplighters.

children.label: → lamplighters
children.gloss: Victorian workers who lit street gas lamps; at dusk with a long pole.

children.label: Victorian workers who lit street gas lamps
children.gloss: Victorian workers who lit street gas lamps

children.label: at dusk with a long pole
children.gloss: at dusk with a long pole

children.label: Parish Books and Headstones
children.gloss: From 1538, parish church registers recorded local baptisms, marriages, and burials, complemented outdoors by carved churchyard headstones.

children.label: parish registers
children.gloss: Church books started in 1538; listing baptisms, weddings, and burials.

children.label: baptisms
children.gloss: Church christening records naming babies,; parents, and fathers’ trades.

children.label: → headstones
children.gloss: Carved churchyard memorials recording names,; death dates, and ages.

children.label: Victorian School Logbooks
children.gloss: From 1862, headteachers wrote weekly School Logbooks recording harvest absences, snowdrifts, illnesses, slate lessons, and inspector visits.

children.label: School Logbooks
children.gloss: Compulsory weekly diaries written by; British headteachers from 1862.

children.label: slate boards
children.gloss: Reusable grey stone writing tablets; used by Victorian pupils.

children.label: → harvests
children.gloss: Autumn farm work that emptied; country classrooms in September.

children.label: 4. How Our Town Earned Its Living
children.q2Chain: Market Halls and Milestones → Canals, Locks and Watermills → Steam Stations and Street Names
children.gloss: Market Halls and Milestones → Canals, Locks and Watermills → Steam Stations and Street Names

children.label: Market Halls and Milestones
children.gloss: Covered market crosses sheltered local farm trade while turnpike trusts smoothed coach roads and set carved stone milestones every mile.

children.label: market crosses
children.gloss: Roofed town shelters where country farmers; sold butter, wool, and grain.

children.label: Roofed town shelters where country farmers
children.gloss: Roofed town shelters where country farmers

children.label: turnpike roads
children.gloss: Main 18th-century toll highways; maintained for horse-drawn coaches.

children.label: → milestones
children.gloss: Carved roadside stones recording exact; miles to towns and London.

children.label: Canals, Locks and Watermills
children.gloss: Fast streams turned mill waterwheels while horse-drawn narrowboats climbed wooden canal locks and iron aqueducts carrying heavy coal and pottery.

children.label: narrowboats
children.gloss: Long, slim cargo boats pulled smoothly; along canals by one horse.

children.label: Long, slim cargo boats pulled smoothly
children.gloss: Long, slim cargo boats pulled smoothly

children.label: canal locks
children.gloss: Water-filled chambers with wooden gates; lifting boats up hills.

children.label: → waterwheels
children.gloss: Giant riverside wheels turning; millstones and textile machinery.

children.label: Steam Stations and Street Names
children.gloss: Victorian steam railways connected British towns until many country branch lines closed in the 1960s, leaving clues in bridges, cycle paths, and street names.

children.label: steam railways
children.gloss: Fast Victorian train lines linking; ports, mines, farms, and cities.

children.label: Station Road
children.gloss: Common street name still pointing to; a live or vanished station.

children.label: Common street name still pointing to
children.gloss: Common street name still pointing to

children.label: → branch lines
children.gloss: Smaller rural train routes, many turned; into walking trails after the 1960s.

children.label: Smaller rural train routes, many turned
children.gloss: Smaller rural train routes, many turned

children.label: 3. Memorials and Living Memory
children.gloss: Village and Town War Memorials → Fabian Ware and Equal Headstones → Tracing One Name to One Street • Oral History and Living Memory → National Trust and Listed Buildings → Designing a Local Heritage Trail

children.label: 5. Names Carved in Stone
children.q2Chain: Village and Town War Memorials → Fabian Ware and Equal Headstones → Tracing One Name to One Street
children.gloss: Village and Town War Memorials → Fabian Ware and Equal Headstones → Tracing One Name to One Street

children.label: Village and Town War Memorials
children.gloss: Because fallen service personnel were buried overseas, British communities built over 100,000 local War Memorials after 1918 and added 1939–1945 names later.

children.label: War Memorials
children.gloss: Local crosses and church; plaques naming fallen neighbours.

children.label: surnames
children.gloss: Family names carved in stone—often; brothers from one street.

children.label: → poppy wreaths
children.gloss: Red Remembrance tributes laid at; local memorials each November.

children.label: Fabian Ware and Equal Headstones
children.gloss: Founded by Fabian Ware in 1917, the War Graves Commission gave generals and privates identical white Portland stone headstones carved with regimental badges.

children.label: Fabian Ware
children.gloss: Red Cross commander who founded the; War Graves Commission in 1917.

children.label: Red Cross commander who founded the
children.gloss: Red Cross commander who founded the

children.label: Portland stone
children.gloss: Pale Dorset limestone used; for uniform CWGC headstones.

children.label: → regiments
children.gloss: County or city army units; whose badges appear on headstones.

children.label: Tracing One Name to One Street
children.gloss: Cross-checking CWGC registers, bronze Memorial Plaques, campaign medals, 1911 Censuses, and wartime newspapers traces one carved name back to a local house.

children.label: memorial plaques
children.gloss: Round bronze WWI medallions cast; with each fallen person’s name.

children.label: service medals
children.gloss: Silver and rainbow campaign ribbons; awarded for wartime service.

children.label: → local newspapers
children.gloss: Wartime town papers printing soldiers’; letters, photos, and tributes.

children.label: 6. Living Memory, Oral History and Saving Local Heritage
children.q2Chain: Oral History and Living Memory → National Trust and Listed Buildings → Designing a Local Heritage Trail
children.gloss: Oral History and Living Memory → National Trust and Listed Buildings → Designing a Local Heritage Trail

children.label: Oral History and Living Memory
children.gloss: Respectful oral history interviews capture post-1945 memories—like corner grocers and pre-1971 shillings—cross-checked against archive photographs.

children.label: oral history
children.gloss: Recording older people’s spoken memories; of everyday past life.

children.label: shillings
children.gloss: Pre-decimal British coins used before; Decimal Day in February 1971.

children.label: → archive photos
children.gloss: Dated street photographs used; to cross-check spoken memories.

children.label: National Trust and Listed Buildings
children.gloss: Ceramic Blue Plaques (from 1866), Octavia Hill’s 1895 National Trust, and 1947 Listed Building laws safeguard Britain’s historic buildings and green spaces.

children.label: Octavia Hill
children.gloss: Social reformer who co-founded the; National Trust in 1895.

children.label: National Trust
children.gloss: Charity protecting historic buildings,; mills, coasts, and countryside.

children.label: → Listed Buildings
children.gloss: Historic structures protected from demolitio; by law since 1947.

children.label: Designing a Local Heritage Trail
children.gloss: Combining place-names, 1880s OS maps, architecture, censuses, War Memorials, and oral history lets pupils design a local Heritage Trail anywhere in the UK.

children.label: Heritage Trails
children.gloss: Mapped walking routes connecting local; historic stops and stories.

children.label: county archives
children.gloss: Free public record offices holding; local maps, censuses, and logbooks.

children.label: → doorstep clues
children.gloss: Everyday street names, postboxes,; benchmarks, and buildings outside.
